core_coverage.answer_quote: Aphelios is a basic-attack-focused marksman who deals mainly physical damage.
core_coverage.reason: Supported as a qualitative synthesis of his role, weapon attacks and physical-damage effects.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Severum's Onslaught grants movement speed, but he has no dash or blink, making positioning important when enemies close in.
core_coverage.reason: The complete supplied active-kit enumeration supports the absence inference; its basis and completeness risk are explicitly recorded outside the card face.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Aphelios equips two of five weapons with distinct attacks and abilities; the main-hand determines his active, and weapon actives have separate cooldowns.
core_coverage.reason: Explains equipment, main-hand selection and the supported independent-cooldown interaction.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Basic attacks and weapon-active casts spend ammunition, but automatic attacks caused by abilities spend no additional ammunition; an empty weapon moves to the queue's end and is replaced by the next reserve weapon.
core_coverage.reason: Explains consumption, the automatic-attack exemption, replacement and queue cycling.

core_coverage.answer_quote: He starts with Calibrum main-hand and Severum off-hand, then Gravitum, Infernum and Crescendum in reserve; E shows the next weapon and can display a text prompt.
core_coverage.reason: Gives the correct starting arrangement and explains E as a display and prompt.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Phase is available from the start, weapon actives unlock at level 2, and Moonlight Vigil unlocks at level 6 and improves at levels 11 and 16; skill points grant attack damage, attack speed or lethality instead of ability ranks.
core_coverage.reason: All unlock levels and alternative skill-point uses match the evidence.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Calibrum grants longer basic attack range while main-hand.
core_coverage.reason: States the range benefit with its main-hand condition.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Calibrum hits through abilities mark enemies for a long-range follow-up with the off-hand weapon, or the main-hand weapon if Calibrum is off-hand. The follow-up consumes all marks and adds physical damage for each mark consumed.
core_coverage.reason: Explains mark creation, weapon dependencies, consumption and bonus damage.

core_coverage.answer_quote: With Calibrum main-hand, Moonshot fires a long-range directional bolt that deals physical damage to the first enemy hit and marks it for a long-range follow-up attack.
core_coverage.reason: Correctly explains selection, first-hit collision, damage and marking.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Severum attacks heal Aphelios, converting excess healing into a shield.
core_coverage.reason: Explains both healing and excess-healing conversion.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Its basic attacks do not use projectiles, and their preparation before the hit cannot be cancelled.
core_coverage.reason: Accurately paraphrases non-projectile attacks and uncancellable windup.

core_coverage.answer_quote: With Severum main-hand, Onslaught grants movement speed and lets Aphelios move while automatically alternating attacks between Severum and his off-hand weapon.
core_coverage.reason: Explains movement, automatic attacks and both weapon dependencies.

core_coverage.answer_quote: It attacks the nearest visible enemy, prioritizing champions.
core_coverage.reason: Matches the sourced targeting rule.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Gravitum basic attacks slow enemies, with the slow weakening over time.
core_coverage.reason: Explains the decaying slow.

core_coverage.answer_quote: With Gravitum main-hand, Binding Eclipse deals magic damage and roots targetable enemies affected by Gravitum's slow.
core_coverage.reason: Explains the general debuff-dependent damage and root with the targetability condition; does not claim that a landed slow is the only cast-enabling circumstance.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Infernum basic attacks deal increased damage to the primary target, damage other enemies along their path, and spread into a cone behind the primary target.
core_coverage.reason: Explains all three core effects without asserting universally lower secondary damage.

core_coverage.answer_quote: With Infernum main-hand, Duskwave deals physical damage in a cone, then follows up against each enemy hit with a delayed off-hand attack.
core_coverage.reason: Explains the cone, delay, affected targets and off-hand dependency without guaranteeing damage through defenses.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Crescendum must return before Aphelios can attack again, and catching it resets his attack timer, favoring close-range attacks with shorter return travel.
core_coverage.reason: Explains the return gate and timer reset; the close-range consequence follows qualitatively from travel distance.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Abilities that would attack with Crescendum instead send returning mirror chakrams; catching them strengthens Crescendum attacks with bonus physical damage based on how many he holds. Catching another mirror chakram or attacking a champion with Crescendum refreshes their duration.
core_coverage.reason: Explains generation, collection, damage scaling and both refresh conditions.

core_coverage.answer_quote: With Crescendum main-hand, Sentry places a stationary sentry that grants sight and automatically attacks the nearest visible enemy in range with a copy of the off-hand weapon.
core_coverage.reason: Explains placement, vision, targeting and off-hand dependence; stationary behavior is a reasonable consequence of the supplied emplacement description.

core_coverage.answer_quote: An enemy entering its range activates it and makes it targetable.
core_coverage.reason: Explains activation and targetability.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Phase swaps Aphelios' main-hand and off-hand weapons, changing his basic attack and available weapon active.
core_coverage.reason: Directly explains the exchange and its consequences.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Moonlight Vigil explodes on an enemy champion, deals physical damage to champions in the area, then follows with physical attacks carrying the main-hand weapon's effect chosen when fired; swapping during flight does not change it.
core_coverage.reason: Explains collision, area damage, follow-up attacks and the sourced weapon-effect lock.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Calibrum applies empowered marks
core_coverage.reason: States the Calibrum outcome.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Severum heals Aphelios through the blast and follow-up attacks
core_coverage.reason: States both healing components in the champion-hit context established by the opening sentence.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Gravitum applies an enhanced slow and lets Binding Eclipse root affected targets for longer.
core_coverage.reason: Explains enhanced slowing and the conditional longer root, supported by the supplied comparison.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Infernum increases the initial blast's damage and makes follow-up attacks splash around targets, with overlapping areas damaging champions
core_coverage.reason: Explains increased blast damage, splash and overlap without relying on disputed formulas.

core_coverage.answer_quote: Crescendum grants mirror chakrams, increasing with the number of targets hit by the initial blast.
core_coverage.reason: Explains generation and target-count dependence at the frozen qualitative level.

conflicts.resolution: E displays the next reserve weapon and can produce a text prompt; this does not establish a third combat spell.

The detailed ammunition rule qualifies the short general description: primary casts and ordinary attacks consume ammunition, while ability-generated automatic attacks consume no additional ammunition.
Retain qualitative ultimate effects. Exclude conflicting formulas, bug reports, pending tests and outdated numerical examples from learned facts.
The explicit in-flight swap rule qualifies the general current-main-weapon wording; teaching the firing weapon's effect is supported.

factual_risks: Dash/blink absence remains an explicitly typed exhaustive-kit inference with a recorded completeness dependency, rather than a confirmed source quotation.

The draft conflict entry mentioning a prior kit_complete=false review has no independently supplied supporting review. Treat that reference as unverified metadata; the supplied live sections support completeness at the requested teaching scope.
Crescendum's close-range advantage and Sentry's stationary characterization are qualitative derivations from supplied mechanics, not verbatim assertions; their metadata discloses this.
Ultimate numerical uncertainty and Binding Eclipse immunity/projectile exceptions remain metadata issues; they do not invalidate the supported qualitative cores.
